clue.text: Items batsmen hit in the air for slip

parts.note: in cricket the batsmen hit balls
something in the air is up

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a ball skied off the bat towards a fielder at slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' is a fielding position in cricket, which fits the batting surface, but here it means a blunder. A BALLS-UP is British slang for a mess or botched job.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a mistake, and a balls-up is a slangy British term for a bungled mistake.

clue.text: Opening new tavern, one invited in

indicators.note: invited in says the single letter is welcomed inside the other piece
new suggests the word tavern is made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A new pub opening its doors to a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TAVERN to ARVENT, which takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An air vent is an opening that lets air in or out.

clue.text: Pole dancing doctor lubed after rotation?

indicators.note: after rotation means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: lubed means oiled, so the doctor is given oil, OIL around him
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A saucy image of a doctor in pole dancing, oiled up and spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole dancing' suggests a strip club; here it is the dance under a pole. OIL, read backwards as LIO, wraps around MB.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which performers lean back to pass under a lowered horizontal bar.

clue.text: Free lunch a figment, ultimately fabricated

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so these letters are built into a new order
ultimately takes the final letter of the word figment

explanation.surface: The saying that there's no such thing as a free lunch: it is a figment.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlatch a door or gate is to free it by lifting its catch.

clue.text: Some chocolate brought over in perfect case of cocoa beans

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: A1 means first-class or perfect, its figure 1 written here as the letter I

indicators.note: brought over suggests the chocolate word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a piece of chocolate

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, the first and last of cocoa

explanation.surface: Chocolate delivered in a perfect box of cocoa beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' is the reversal signal; 'in' puts the turned chocolate inside A1, the figure 1 standing for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is the most widely grown species of coffee plant, so its beans are a kind of bean.

clue.text: Begin again on problem, last of three

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: last of picks the closing letter of the word three

explanation.surface: Restarting work on the third of three problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to start again after a pause.

clue.text: One of billions vacuous buffoon, I recall, wasted?

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked, so these letters are scattered into a new order
vacuous means empty, so the word buffoon is emptied of its inner letters

explanation.surface: An empty-headed fool, perhaps from drink, may have just one brain cell left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' leaves BN from 'buffoon'; with I and RECALL that makes BNIRECALL, which 'wasted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The human brain contains tens of billions of neurons, so a brain cell is one among billions.

clue.text: Correct catches fitting trap

indicators.note: catches says the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: to cure is to put right, correct
apt means fitting

explanation.surface: Adjusting a trap that keeps catching things.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture is to seize or catch, as a trap does.

clue.text: Condiment male put with hotcake when cooking

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so tom means male

indicators.note: when cooking suggests the words put and hotcake are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man adding sauce to a pancake on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato ketchup is a sauce served as a condiment with food.

clue.text: See 17
Seems towelling filled with poo, shake a leg!

parts.note: looks means seems or appears
a used towelling nappy (diaper) is filled with poo

explanation.surface: A toilet-humour command urging someone with a soiled towel to get a move on.
explanation.walkthrough: A nappy is the British word for a diaper, traditionally made of towelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms urging someone to hurry up: shake a leg and look snappy mean move quickly.

clue.text: Relax, militant carnivore's cry?

definitions.meaning: a militant meat-eater might cry for vegetables to be thrown out

explanation.surface: A relaxed meat-eater with a battle cry against vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax by lounging idly is the slang sense; read as two words it is a meat-lover's slogan banishing vegetables.

clue.text: It's positively charged, reporting uproar after getting 24 across?

indicators.note: the answer is what comes after the other entry once that is taken off the front
reporting signals that the sound of a spoken word is what counts

parts.note: pandemonium is wild uproar
the answer to 24 across is PANNED

explanation.surface: A question about an ion that, said with the right word in front, makes a great commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Say PANNED (the 24 across answer) followed by the answer and it sounds like PANDEMONIUM; remove the PANNED that comes first to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ammonium ion carries a positive charge, being formed when ammonia gains a proton.

clue.text: Too sad, the fragments belonging to a nation

indicators.note: fragments of the words, broken up, are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A melancholy view of a broken-up nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose in grammar: statehood is the condition of belonging to, or being, a nation state.
explanation.definitionFit: Statehood is the status of being a recognised state, a condition of nationhood.

clue.text: Check suit, where kit should be white

parts.note: to test is to check
to suit is to match, go well with

explanation.surface: A dress code check: is the outfit suitably white?
explanation.walkthrough: In Test cricket, the international game between nations, players traditionally wear all-white clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a cricket fixture played in traditional white clothing, where kit means sports outfit.

clue.text: See 27
Nostalgic memory of Vesuvius (AD79)

definitions.meaning: something that brings back nostalgic memories
the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79, which buried Pompeii

explanation.surface: Fond recollection of the volcano that destroyed Pompeii.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a reminder of old times; taken literally it is an explosion from history, as the eruption was.

clue.text: Sentry found nothing right in hooligan

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces sit inside the hooligan word

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
O is the figure nought, nothing
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A guard who finds no problem with a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a person posted to keep watch, as a sentry does.

clue.text: Brew drink in fresh coffee, finally

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky means pert
cola is a soft drink

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word coffee

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a drink from freshly brewed coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the coffee, but here it means cheeky, as in a fresh remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate is to make coffee by passing boiling water through grounds, a way to brew it.

clue.text: Nick grabs dance

parts.note: cops means grabs or catches
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A man called Nick grabbing a partner for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for a police station (and for arrest), and a cop shop is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the nick is the police station, which is also called the cop shop.

clue.text: See 17
Poles securing trained part of plant

indicators.note: securing says the poles hold the other piece fast between them

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
tame means trained or domesticated

explanation.surface: Poles used to hold up a trained climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-bearing male organ of a flower.

clue.text: Being from another planet burrowed into immense surface

indicators.note: burrowed into says the alien has dug its way inside the other word

parts.note: cosmic means vast or immense
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: A sci-fi image of an alien tunnelling into a huge surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic means superficial, concerning only the outside appearance of something.

clue.text: Laid back, office siesta criticised

indicators.note: laid back here means put backwards, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: a den is a study or private office
a siesta is a nap

explanation.surface: A relaxed office worker criticised for a nap at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' looks like the casual adjective, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be panned is to be harshly criticised, as by reviewers.

clue.text: Finish off queen after uprising in African country

indicators.note: after uprising, in a down clue, means the letters are read from the bottom up
finish off means the final letter is cut away

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A revolution ending with the queen's overthrow in an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African country.

clue.text: Daft trap for one using foul language

parts.note: potty is British slang for daft or crazy
trap is slang for mouth

explanation.surface: A silly trap set for someone who swears.
explanation.definitionFit: A potty mouth is someone who habitually swears or speaks crudely.

clue.text: 'Stick with knob', one stripping discussed?

indicators.note: discussed signals spoken words, so it is how they sound that counts

parts.note: a stripper is leaving behind the clothes, or kit, worn: so one who leaves clothes

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a stripper and a stick with a knob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' is slang for clothes, so a stripper is a 'gear leaver'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gear lever, or gearstick, is the knobbed stick a driver uses to change gear.

clue.text: Initially scratched, attractive print

indicators.note: initially scratched says the opening letter is struck out

parts.note: fetching means attractive

explanation.surface: An attractive print, slightly scratched at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from a plate whose design is eaten into it by acid.

clue.text: Talk about exercise in run

indicators.note: about says the talking word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to orate is to talk at length
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Chatting about exercise while out running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is the definition, as in run a business, not jogging.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine or business is to run it.
